runtime_workloads.label: startup
runtime_workloads.description: process startup and exit of a trivial program

runtime_workloads.label: integer-computation
runtime_workloads.description: a tight integer arithmetic reduction (sum 1..=1000 by recursion)

runtime_workloads.label: indirect-calls
runtime_workloads.description: a hot loop calling through a first-class function value (ADR-0008 Tier 1) — the indirect-call sibling of function-calls, measured against a C peer calling through a function pointer

runtime_workloads.label: collections
runtime_workloads.description: bulk construction, indexed lookups, and scans over the builtin fixed-size array `[Int; N]` (ADR-0004 Stage 2), the v0 collection

runtime_workloads.label: string-processing
runtime_workloads.description: byte-level tokenizing, scanning, and slice comparison over the borrowed `Str` (ADR-0006): space/slash/digit counts and method/version slice checks over a fixed request-log line

runtime_workloads.label: allocation
runtime_workloads.description: heap allocation and deallocation throughput over the ADR-0009 allocator core: a growable `Array[Int]` and an owned `String`, each built by repeated push/append (doubling growth) and freed at scope end, over many rounds

runtime_workloads.label: map-lookup
runtime_workloads.description: keyed insert/lookup/churn throughput over the ADR-0011 hash map `Map[Int, Int]`: 1000 inserts (doubling table growth), 1000 lookups summed modulo 1000, and 500 removals per round, over many rounds

runtime_workloads.label: file-io
runtime_workloads.description: effect-crossing throughput over the ADR-0013 OS boundary: per round, open/write/close a 240-byte scratch file, reopen and read it back byte-at-a-time through the read_byte seam, and remove it — the deferred ADR-0006 effect-crossing benchmark, measured against a C peer making the identical open/write/read/close/unlink calls

runtime_workloads.label: networking
runtime_workloads.description: a basic socket round-trip over the ADR-0014 socket effects: per round, listen on an ephemeral loopback port, connect to it, accept, send 128 bytes from the client, read them back on the server byte-at-a-time through the read_byte seam, and close all three descriptors — measured against C and Go peers making the identical calls

runtime_workloads.label: channels
runtime_workloads.description: synchronization-crossing throughput over the ADR-0015 channel primitives: per round, send 500 values through one process-lived channel and receive all 500 back — single-threaded so the number isolates the locked-FIFO crossing itself — measured against a C peer making the identical mutex-and-condvar crossings and a Go peer using its native buffered channel

runtime_workloads.label: json-parse
runtime_workloads.description: JSON decoding throughput over the ADR-0016 data increment: per round, recursive-descent parse of a fixed 149-byte document into an Array[Int]/Array[Float] kind/number arena, folding a structural checksum (3 × nodes + the truncated number sum) — measured against a strtod-based C peer making the identical walk and Go's standard encoding/json (the parity target) walking to the same checksum

runtime_workloads.label: sha256-hash
runtime_workloads.description: cryptographic hashing throughput over the ADR-0019 bitwise operators: per round, the full FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 compression function over a fixed 64-byte message (two padded blocks), every hash word combined with a masked modular add since a bare `+` traps on the carry a checksum requires — measured against a uint32_t C peer making the identical rotations and shifts and Go's standard crypto/sha256 (the parity target). This workload could not be written before ADR-0019 Stage A: SHA-256 is *defined* in rotations, xors, and shifts, so without them it has no expression at all

runtime_workloads.label: wire-decode
runtime_workloads.description: binary protocol framing throughput over the ADR-0019 bitwise operators: per round, walk a fixed 256-byte buffer of 16 length-prefixed frames, decoding a big-endian 4-byte length and 2-byte type per frame, re-encoding the length to verify the round-trip, and folding the payload — the shape of every binary wire protocol, and the concrete PostgreSQL message header ADR-0019 was opened for — measured against a uint32_t C peer making the identical shifts and masks and a Go peer using encoding/binary's BigEndian.Uint32/PutUint32 (the parity target)

runtime_workloads.label: udp-echo
runtime_workloads.description: datagram round-trip throughput over the ADR-0017 UDP effects: per round, bind two ephemeral loopback UDP sockets, then for each of 8 datagrams send 16 bytes, receive the message (whose boundary udp_recv reports), read all 16 bytes back through udp_byte_at, and echo a reply to the port udp_peer_port names — measured against a sendto/recvfrom C peer and a Go peer using net.ListenPacket/WriteTo/ReadFrom (the parity target)

runtime_workloads.label: connect-timeout
runtime_workloads.description: the cost of a bounded failure over the ADR-0017 timeout effects: per round, connect_timeout to a loopback port nothing listens on and require the attempt to come back — refused or timed out — rather than hang. This workload could not be written before ADR-0017, since a blocking connect has no bounded outcome; measured against a non-blocking connect+poll C peer and a Go peer using net.DialTimeout, both with the same deadline
